raw_response:
I would start with **Brevo** for a small community project, and choose **Amazon SES** if the lowest running cost matters enough to justify AWS onboarding. Both have a documented API route that avoids hosting or configuring your own SMTP server. Brevo documents a direct HTTPS request; SES explicitly supports its API as an alternative to SMTP. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn335155212view3","turn184566086view1"]}}

The missing number is your busiest day's volume. “Thousands of emails” could mean a few thousand spread across a month, or a few thousand immediately after a local event. I would not assume a monthly free allowance can absorb the latter.

## Ranked shortlist

| Rank | Service | Verified cost or allowance | When I would choose it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Brevo](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/send-a-transactional-email) | Free: 300 sends/day. Starter begins at $9/month with a 5,000-send tier and no daily sending cap. | A practical starting point for a few thousand messages, using Free only when every day's volume fits. Its plan also lists contact-storage allowances, so check those if you will use Brevo's contact database. |
| 2 | [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) | A-la-carte outbound sending: $0.10/1,000, so approximately $1 for 10,000 recipient deliveries before data and optional-feature charges. | Lowest verified marginal sending price in this comparison, when you can handle AWS setup and obtain production access. |
| 3 | [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing.md) | Free: 3,000/month and 100/day. Pro: $20/month for 50,000 with no daily cap. | A small project that fits both free limits, or one that values the documented SDK integration enough to pay the larger minimum. |
| 4 | [Postmark](https://postmarkapp.com/pricing/) | Basic: $15/month for 10,000; additional usage at $1.80/1,000. Free: only 100/month. | A paid transactional service where 45-day activity retention and delivery diagnostics are useful. |
| 5 | [Zoho ZeptoMail / Zoho CPaaS email](https://www.zoho.com/zeptomail/pricing.html) | The live page confirms 10,000-email credits valid for six months, but the dollar amount was not readable. | An additional option for irregular sending, pending a current price and account-terms check. |

The figures above come from the providers' own pages. Brevo's allowance and entry tier, Resend's monthly and daily limits, and Postmark's paid starting tier were readable directly. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn364327763view2","turn233461305view0","turn335155212view1"]}} SES's $1 example is arithmetic from the published a-la-carte sending rate, not an all-in quotation. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn184566086view0"}} Zoho's old pricing URL now redirects to CPaaS; that live page confirms the credit structure but does not substantiate a current dollar price. I would not rely on the older amount still shown in a search excerpt. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn335155212view2","turn238896710search2"]}}

## What the choice entails

**Brevo is my default recommendation under the information supplied.** Use its HTTPS transactional endpoint with an API key and a configured sender/domain. The endpoint contains `smtp` in its path, but the documented integration is an HTTP API call; it does not ask you to run an SMTP server. If your project might send more than 300 messages in a day, budget for a suitable paid tier from the outset. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn335155212view3","turn364327763view2"]}}

**SES is the cost-first alternative.** New accounts begin in a sandbox limited to verified recipients, 200 messages per 24 hours and one message per second. Production access is a separate approval step, and you still verify your sending identities. That makes it worth testing onboarding before depending on SES for a real community launch. These are account and sending-domain tasks, which differ from the custom SMTP server work you want to avoid. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn184566086view2","turn184566086view1"]}} The current pricing page also says new accounts default to Essentials from July 21, 2026, at $0.16/1,000; you can switch to a-la-carte. Check the active plan instead of assuming every account starts at $0.10/1,000. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn184566086view0"}}

**Resend is attractive if the free limits genuinely fit.** Its official SDK example sends through the API with an API key and requires verification when using your own domain. A single busy day can be the reason to leave Free even when the monthly total is below 3,000. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn233461305view1","turn233461305view0"]}} Its pricing FAQ offers an application process for registered nonprofits to receive 50% off paid plans. A noncommercial local project is not automatically a registered nonprofit, so I have not assumed that discount. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn364327763view3"}}

For “reliable,” the evidence here establishes documented delivery interfaces and operational features, not comparative inbox-placement results. Postmark lists activity retention, analytics and delivery/bounce information; those help investigate missing messages, but they do not prove that it will outperform the others for your recipients. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn335155212view1"}} My practical next step would be to send a representative pilot, inspect failures and delivery events, and compare the actual daily peak with the selected plan. No production integration or delivery experiment was performed in this research.

This review used live public material retrieved on November 21, 2026. The input question is dated June 1, 2026. Several pages are undated, and the SES default-plan change is explicitly later than the question; these figures should therefore be read as the observed current offerings, not a reconstructed June 1 price list.
